grandparents_cupboard.reason: Flour, butter, sugar, milk, redcurrants, lemon and Greek yoghurt are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Redcurrant punnets are in mainstream supermarkets in July, and everything else is an everyday staple.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a bowl and a baking tray are needed, and rubbing in and patting out a scone round is beginner technique.

works.reason: The flour, butter and milk ratios suit a single scone round. 220°C for 15 to 18 minutes is right for a 3cm-thick round, and eight wedges with yoghurt suit four people.

honest_times.reason: Stripping 150g of currants and rubbing in the butter fits in 15 minutes, and the 18 minutes of cooking matches the bake time in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the lemon used as zest, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Redcurrants are the main fruit in a summer afternoon scone, which suits late July.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short and plain British English, and a cook would read the 3cm round as its thickness.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a modestly sweetened fruit scone served with yoghurt, a sensible family snack.
